speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: asked the Minister for Health in view of the global increase in measles cases reported by the World Health Organization, what measures are in place to prevent measles outbreaks in Singapore and whether these measures need to be strengthened further.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: High vaccination coverage at the population level not only protects the individuals but also makes it harder for the disease to spread, thereby reducing the risk of large outbreaks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This way, it provides herd immunity which will also protect those who are unable to receive vaccination, such as infants under the age of 12 months and those who are immune-compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is, therefore, important for countries to maintain a high level of vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In recent years, there has been a global increase in measles outbreaks because of declining vaccination coverage in many countries.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This has resulted in a significant increase of non-immune individuals in the community, making it easier for the disease to spread.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Being a travel hub, Singapore is also exposed to imported cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These were all sporadic cases or cases with limited spread and there was no community outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are monitoring the global and local situation closely.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have alerted our doctors to look out for measles cases and notify the Ministry of Health (MOH) promptly so that actions can be taken to prevent disease spread.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should also strive to achieve a high level of vaccination in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our national immunisation schedule recommends that children should have their first dose of measles vaccine at 12 months of age and the second dose at 15 to 18 months of age.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With the exception of those who are unable to be vaccinated because of medical reasons, the measles vaccine is compulsory for local children.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have also put in place measures to facilitate and encourage vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Vaccination is available free to all Singaporean children at polyclinics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) sends reminders to parents whose children have yet to complete vaccination by two years old.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: HPB also provides catch-up vaccination in primary and secondary schools for students who still have not completed their vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH is looking into ways to raise the vaccination coverage further.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of the measures being considered include sending reminders to parents ahead of vaccination due dates.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This way, we ensure that children are protected as early as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also look into how we can raise the vaccination rate of children before they enter preschool and primary school.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even with these measures, we can continue to have sporadic cases of measles due to imported cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We can expect to see more cases when there is an increase in global outbreaks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: By working together to improve and maintain a high level of vaccination coverage, we can better protect our population and reduce the risk of large local outbreaks.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The first is with regard to the measles cases that were reported recently, that is, the increase to 43 cases.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could I just maybe have an understanding of the type of cases?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Just to get a feel of how these cases arose.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second question is with regard to vaccination rates.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I note the answer on the vaccination rates with regard to children.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I was wondering whether we have data on the overall vaccination rate for the resident population in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is because if we look at the outbreaks overseas, a lot of cases arose in adults and so on, not just in the paediatric community.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The third supplementary question: I was wondering whether we have some ideas or some knowledge about what are the reasons that certain children or adults refuse to be vaccinated.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think this maybe comes with the next Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry think that the anti-vaccination movement and the online misinformation have an important impact on the reason why parents, or maybe adults even, are refusing the vaccination?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The last supplementary question is regarding whether MOH foresees that in the event of an outbreak or even pre-emptively, actions might be taken against unvaccinated individuals?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We have seen in other countries there are restrictions on children who are unvaccinated from attending preschool or even going to school.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The German Minister for Health has just proposed that there might be financial penalties for people who are unvaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Ten were vaccinated but, as all of us know, vaccination may not be 100% effective.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we need to raise the overall population coverage to protect the small number of people who are unprotected despite vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Among those who were not vaccinated, nine of them were infants before they were due for vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The rest were aged between one and 54.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, there is a wide variation of ages.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For the adults, we do not have specific data on how many of them were vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But there was a recent study in 2018 on seroprevalence.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The study indicated that the vast majority of adults in Singapore had a very high level of immunity against measles.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: One of the possible reasons could be that in the early 1970s, measles was very widespread, a very common occurrence, and many of us who are adults could remember having measles during that time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, the naturally acquired immunity arising from actually contracting measles is prevalent among adults.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu also asked about the reasons why some of them did not go for vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: A large majority of them were just passive, waiting for the next convenient occasion to bring their children for vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They hope that the next time when they see a doctor, they can bring their children, but their children stayed healthy, so never had a chance to see the doctor.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When they do see the doctor, the children may be unwell and, therefore, not suitable for vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we would like to encourage parents, if possible, to bring your children for vaccination as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: HPB does conduct vaccination programmes in the schools to provide convenience for parents to have their children vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Especially in infant care, many of them are below 12 months of age and they could not be vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, the older children ought to be vaccinated to protect them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, we are also looking at workers in the preschool sector to ensure that they are covered by vaccination or they have immunity, so as to protect the children under their charge.
